title: Any tips on optimising token usage across Codex and Claude?
author: No_Degree_8837
selftext:
I’ve been developing games with AI for a few years now, I started back in 2022 copy pasting ChatGPT to VS Code! Mostly just for fun and experimenting. More recently (this past year) I’ve focused on one game idea and really put my head into it. It’s been great so far.

However, I’ve noticed recently that I’m burning through my usage much much quicker than I was maybe a month or so ago - and I’m wondering if it’s something fixable?

It could be just down to a much larger codebase, poor prompting ect, but I’m wondering if anyone has any tips?

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body:
The providers keep messing with the useage limits, however, optimization is always a good idea. 

The best thing IMO is to have a modular architecture, work on each slice seperatly, avoid running long-context tasks and seperate them into smaller tasks instead, higher context is billed at a higher rate.

Reasoning levels matter, throwing lower reasoning at a task that is complex would net you with more tokens used to complete it, while higher reasoning for tasks that don't justify it would be practically wasting tokens. This is sadly not something that can be generalized as in use X reason for Y task, you'd have to figure this bit out based on your experience with the models.

Ask your agent for optimization tips, it has a better undeerstanding of your workflow than us random redditors.

Hope that helps.

replies.author: No_Degree_8837
replies.body:
Thanks, yeah I think I need to take a break from implementation and tweaking and use some tokens on optimising my workflow. Thanks for the reply!

I did have a suspicion that usage limits had been meddled with too

comments.author: Reditoxaz
comments.body:
Talking there only about claude-code.

Id start with basics, how caching works, how sub agents works, how does ur [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) look like and other related documents that AI has to read? Claude also keep memoriess which can pile up. Installing stupid SKILLs you see online those 100k+ star repos can easily eat 10-20k context even if you do not invoke them because their descriptions enter context, note: theyre useless.



Turn off artifact tool in claude-code (saves 13k tokens) if you want to keep it you can turn it off for sub agents, This applies to even built-in general purpose sub agent he still has the artifact tool in its list....

Watch your cache expiry -> Main chat you have open is cached for 1 hour after that you miss the cache.

Turning off claude-skill sync is also handy in my case saving 6k tokens

never go above 600k context, even if you have warm cache it gets expensive.

Tell claude to analyze past chats and look for instances when agent wasn't chaining commands whenever he could -> this again can save some tokens

Sub agents have cache by default at 5minutes, if your sub agent is running long loops/waits he periodically hit cache miss and u pay for whole context. I actually plan to ship all those tips as CLI but its not finished yet.

comments.author: johnv_dev
comments.body: usually it's the codebase growing. every message resends the whole chat plus every file it opened, so a long session on a big project gets expensive fast. what helped me most was starting a fresh chat for each task and telling it exactly which files to look at, so it isn't crawling the whole project every time.
